title: CoinRun PPO official-recipe parity control
question: Does a from-scratch JAX PPO control aligned to the public Procgen easy-200 recipe recover the approximately 8.7-9.0 mean CoinRun return shown near 25M steps in the official paper?
reason: CR-PPO-0001 completed correctly at the systems level but reached only 4.96 mean return on a post-hoc 512-episode stochastic full-distribution evaluation. Source comparison found four training/evaluation implementation deviations from the public reference recipe, so another dynamics dataset must not be authorized until a parity control distinguishes an implementation problem from normal variance.
hypothesis: Changing only the reference-recipe mismatches—200 training levels, discounted-return normalization gamma 0.99, per-minibatch advantage normalization, TensorFlow-default Glorot IMPALA backbone initialization, and stochastic full-distribution evaluation—will produce final 512-episode mean return at least 8.0 and success rate at least 0.80.
falsification: Reject the parity hypothesis if the final 25,165,824-step checkpoint has full-distribution stochastic mean return below 8.0 or success rate below 0.80; treat the result as partial rather than strict reproduction because the framework and Procgen release still differ from the 2019 TensorFlow reference.

source.source_freeze: The executable implementation was committed and pushed before the GPU launch, then checked out as a clean detached DSW worktree at a4d2574b9b25854b72e0a305d8aa1eb299fb3095. Later ledger edits do not change that running source.

compute.estimated_budget: 25,165,824 environment transitions, 24 periodic 128-episode evaluations, and one final 512-episode evaluation; expected wall time is approximately 80-110 minutes based on CR-PPO-0001.
compute.shutdown_policy: Reused only the existing A10. At launch the prior bounded timer was still due at 2026-07-31T00:14:45+08:00 with roughly 9.7 hours remaining, so it was not extended.

reference.target_reading: The official easy-200 CoinRun test curve is visually approximately 8.7-9.0 mean return near 25M environment steps; the plot-derived value is not a machine-readable exact target.

model.backbone_kernel_initializer: Glorot uniform to match tf.layers defaults used by build_impala_cnn

evaluation.visuals: Four bounded full-episode GIFs and a contact sheet at every milestone

known_confounders: The original public reference is TensorFlow/OpenAI Baselines while this control is JAX/Flax/Optax.
The runtime uses Procgen 0.10.7 rather than the older package revision used for the 2019 paper.
Only seed 0 is run; the paper curve aggregates multiple runs.
The numeric reference target is read from a published figure rather than an exported table.

success_criteria.rule: The final checkpoint exists after exactly 25,165,824 environment transitions and its structured run evidence records the exact execution commit and runtime identity.
The final stochastic full-distribution evaluation contains exactly 512 episodes, mean_return >= 8.0, and success_rate >= 0.80.
The zero-step baseline, all 24 periodic milestones, and the separate final evaluation retain metrics plus bounded visual evidence.
No trajectory collection, dynamics training, behavior cloning, or policy training inside a learned world is started under this experiment ID.
